principles: Resolve every user-requested capability row explicitly; no silent partial completion.
Prefer mechanical tests and gate evidence over prose claims.
Retire removed capabilities plainly instead of preserving misleading future backlog.
Keep diagnostic surfaces diagnostic unless code and config enforce them.
Preserve experiment evidence unless a guard proves it is invalid.
drivers: Seven capability rows span docs, gates, status projections, and proof admissibility semantics.
Authority Server has been removed and must not be restored as an active system.
B-c004 should validate whether B-5082-style intent totality prevents milestone shrinkage.

options.name: A: Audit-first closure with red/diagnostic tests, then implement or retire each row
pros: Directly matches the user request to verify need or prior coverage before implementation
Creates evidence for each of the seven rows
Allows removed capabilities to be retired without pretending they are implemented
cons: Requires more PLAN and evidence work than a narrow code patch
May determine that some rows should be non-goals rather than new runtime features

options.name: B: Implement all seven rows as runtime features immediately
pros: Could close some partial rows quickly
cons: Risks reintroducing Authority Server or overbuilding future/non-goal rows
Does not prove existing coverage before mutation
Could preserve the original failure mode where checklist completion diverges from user intent

options.name: C: Documentation-only cleanup
cons: Would not satisfy rows that need tests or runtime enforcement
Would not verify queue/runtime/CommandSpec/waterline behavior mechanically

chosen: A: Audit-first closure with red/diagnostic tests, then implement or retire each row
rationale: Option A is the only option that preserves the seven-row user intent while avoiding both silent shrinkage and unnecessary restoration of retired Authority Server work.

preMortem.scenario: A row is marked done because docs say partial/future rather than because behavior is resolved.
preMortem.trigger: Checklist status is updated before red/diagnostic evidence exists.
preMortem.consequence: The story repeats the M0-M9 failure pattern and leaves hidden partial capabilities.
preMortem.mitigation: Do not mark any checklist item done until it has row-specific test or docs evidence and is bound to verificationIntent.

preMortem.scenario: Authority Server vocabulary cleanup accidentally removes valid legacy compatibility constants or reintroduces server requirements.
preMortem.trigger: A broad search-and-replace changes code enums or docs without considering consumer compatibility.
preMortem.consequence: Existing proof admissibility tests break or docs again imply a removed server capability.
preMortem.mitigation: Use targeted wording: legacy/local/shadow compatibility remains, active Authority Server conformance is retired.

preMortem.scenario: Runtime enforcement is globally claimed but config remains warn or unsafe to enforce by default.
preMortem.trigger: Status/docs are updated without checking enforce-mode behavior.
preMortem.consequence: Users believe DEV/DONE gates are hard-blocking when they are only diagnostic.
preMortem.mitigation: Test warn and enforce paths separately, and document rollback/default status precisely.

preMortem.scenario: Tier-C cleanup deletes or misclassifies experiment evidence.
preMortem.trigger: Duplicate cleanup logic ignores Tier-C experiment exceptions.
preMortem.consequence: Evidence from provider-execution experiments is lost or misreported.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep valid Tier-C experiment rows preserved and only classify malformed/spoofed rows as cleanup-required.
